description: Mara Venn repaired paths for people she never met and crossed out her own name when the work held. The island remembers useful places, then leaves their story to the players who keep them alive.
quests.subtitle: Orientation · A persistent world
quests.title: Island Charter

description: A visible boundary lets neighbors build close without guessing where welcome ends. Public works need a named entrance and an owner so protection never becomes an accidental locked door.
quests.subtitle: Required · Land and public access
quests.title: Claim Clearly

description: A feud is only worth continuing when yesterday's work still exists tomorrow. Consent, claim safety, and an immediate stop keep competition memorable instead of exhausting.
quests.subtitle: Required · Conflict and pranks

tasks.title: I agree to stop on request

quests.title: Rivalry With Consent

description: An FTB Team joins quest progress to claimed ground and shared rewards. Choose it deliberately; a team is a promise about who may finish, claim, and maintain work together.
quests.subtitle: Required · Shared progress
quests.title: Choose Teammates

description: The charter is deliberately small: protect lasting work, ask before rivalry, and know who shares your progress. Once those promises are settled, every calling remains visible and the island can grow in directions nobody planned.
quests.subtitle: Required · Protect · consent · share
quests.title: Sign the Charter

description: Transformation changes a body; a calling changes what someone chooses to maintain. The House, the Order, and the Free Companies each offer a useful place in the world without forbidding curiosity about the others.
quests.subtitle: Identity · Night, lantern, or civic
quests.title: Three Callings

description: Nightbound players trade daylight ease for hunger, speed, and a new obligation to prepare safe rooms after sunset. The House values restraint because appetite without hospitality leaves no neighbors worth knowing.
quests.subtitle: Vampire · Nightbound route
quests.title: Join the House

description: A civic calling keeps workshops, roads, trade, and shelter outside faction demands. Its authority comes from services anyone can use and the quiet power to refuse a feud.
quests.subtitle: Free Company · Shared services
quests.title: Join the Commons

description: Hunters accept specialized tools and the responsibility to make danger legible before striking it. The Order's best patrols leave behind wards, remedies, and a route home—not trophies.
quests.subtitle: Hunter · Lantern route
quests.title: Join the Order

description: A first calling gives the world a place to start, not a wall around the others. Workshops, archives, and public events remain open so players can understand one another's craft.
quests.subtitle: Complete any one calling
quests.title: Keep Doors Open

description: Tamsin Rook keeps a bent stake above the research table, not as a victory but as proof that poor preparation follows people home. A complete field bench gives the next patrol time to think before the door opens.
quests.subtitle: Core I · A working field bench
quests.title: Salt and Steel

description: A refuge becomes trustworthy when its remedies are stocked before anyone needs them. Holy preparation here means stewardship: clean water, clear labels, and enough reserve for the stranger who arrives after the patrol.
quests.subtitle: Core II · Remedies and wards
quests.title: Consecrated Work

description: The Order measures a patrol by how safely it can hand the next watch to someone else. Reliable quarrels and a maintained weapon table turn one veteran's skill into equipment the whole refuge can understand.
quests.subtitle: Core III · Ranged fieldcraft
quests.title: Long Watch

description: Tamsin's last rule is simple: power belongs where it can be accounted for. The enhanced axe hangs beside a ledger of every time it left the refuge and whether it returned clean.
quests.subtitle: Optional mastery · Enhanced fieldcraft
quests.title: Bright Oath

description: Sister Aveline's manual begins with triage, not triumph. A spellwright who can heal, recall, and strike with restraint makes every expedition less dependent on whichever veteran happened to log in first.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Holy support magic
quests.title: Mercy Manual

description: A watchpost should be recognizable in bad weather and easy to repair with ordinary stock. This palette establishes the language; the expanded supply can become a tower, refuge, wall, or roadside ward chosen by its builders.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Outpost palette
quests.title: Stone Lantern

description: A photograph can warn a neighbor without crossing their boundary or turning rumor into accusation. The ledger gives the Order evidence it can discuss, archive, and eventually admit was wrong.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Claim-safe reconnaissance
quests.title: Field Ledger

description: No refuge should depend on a single expert. Two practiced specialties are enough to make the Order resilient while leaving room for later players to adopt the third.
quests.subtitle: Breadth · Core plus any two specialties
quests.title: Two Lanterns

description: Tamsin keeps one lodestone unengraved for the refuge that will outlive its founders. Its eventual name should belong to the stranger who finds shelter there when no officer is online.
quests.subtitle: Team capstone · Mark a public refuge
quests.title: Lantern Charter

description: Ilyas Venn labels every bottle with a donor, a date, or the word unknown. Hunger becomes governable when supply is visible, and a prepared room lets restraint survive the hour when it matters.
quests.subtitle: Core I · Stored blood and shelter
quests.title: First Thirst

description: An altar is not a shortcut around consequence. Pedestals, storage, and measured ingredients turn inheritance into a repeatable craft that another player can inspect instead of a secret only one veteran understands.
quests.subtitle: Core II · Ritual infrastructure
quests.title: Red Measure

description: A weapon with a lineage is still a tool that someone must maintain. The House treats its edge as shared responsibility: enough stock for repair, no mystery about where its strength came from.
quests.subtitle: Core III · Controlled armament
quests.title: Inherited Edge

description: Ilyas calls the enhanced blade a debt made visible. Its scabbard bears the names of three people who may demand it be put away, including one who is not nightbound.
quests.subtitle: Optional mastery · Enhanced bloodwork
quests.title: Night's Due

description: The House writes blood magic as memory before it writes it as violence. Movement, recovery, and measured siphoning let a spellwright protect a night route without reducing every problem to damage.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Blood utility magic
quests.title: Scarlet Script

description: A manor earns its name from the number of people who can find a safe door, not the height of its walls. This palette can become a crypt, guest hall, garden court, or night clinic chosen by its builders.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Manor palette
quests.title: House of Doors

description: Nessa Vale once delivered a sealed letter three days late because she refused to cross a sleeping farm uninvited. The route took longer; the trust it preserved became a road everyone still used.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Safe night routes
quests.title: Moon Courier

description: A house becomes fragile when one person holds every useful secret. Two practiced specialties are enough to share responsibility while leaving a third role open for a later arrival.
quests.subtitle: Breadth · Core plus any two specialties
quests.title: Two Seals

description: Ilyas keeps one lodestone wrapped in a guest's old scarf. It waits for a refuge whose door can be found, whose service can be named, and whose keeper can be questioned when something fails.
quests.subtitle: Team capstone · Mark a night refuge
quests.title: Night Charter

description: Mirelle Quill refuses to call a price fair until both people can read it. A visible vendor and written banking guide turn surplus into choice without asking one grinder to become the server's permanent shopkeeper.
quests.subtitle: Core I · Trade people can inspect
quests.title: Open Ledger

description: The first windmill proved the settlement could turn weather into work. Mirelle's creek line is deliberately plainer: exposed shafts, labeled direction, and a second source another player can diagnose when the wind workshop is busy.
quests.subtitle: Core II · Power beyond the windmill

tasks.title: A teammate traced the power line

quests.title: Second Current

description: A press beside a basin can save eight players from building eight half-finished sheds. The line matters because its inputs are obvious, its output has a chest, and someone can repair it after its founder leaves.
quests.subtitle: Core III · Shared processing

tasks.title: A teammate ran one public recipe

quests.title: Public Line

description: Mirelle calls a machine complete when someone else can use it without waking the builder. Storage, routing, and a public display turn motion into a durable service instead of a personal monument.
quests.subtitle: Optional mastery · Maintainable automation
quests.title: Common Engine

description: A map room turns one person's dangerous discovery into everybody's informed choice. Photographs preserve what coordinates forget: entrances, hazards, and whether the road was kind to travelers.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Exploration archive
quests.title: Map Room

description: A hall needs no grand design to matter. Beds for guests, a bell people can find, and labeled storage make villagers and players part of the same settlement instead of scenery around private bases.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · A simple civic room
quests.title: Village Hall

description: A market works when players can tell what is offered, what it costs, and where the purchase will appear. The clock is less about urgency than confidence that a promised trade will still make sense tomorrow.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Prices and pickup
quests.title: Market Clock

description: The most impressive road is the one a late arrival can follow at night. Durable surface, clear turns, and ordinary repair stock let a route earn trust one uneventful journey at a time.
quests.subtitle: Specialty · Legible public routes
quests.title: Road Keeper

description: The Free Companies refuse the myth of the indispensable founder. Two practiced services are enough to keep the commons useful while leaving a visible vacancy for the next player who wants a role.
quests.subtitle: Breadth · Core plus any two specialties
quests.title: Three Hands

description: Mirelle's spare lodestone carries a brass plate with three blank lines: service, supplies, maintainer. It belongs wherever neutrality becomes something both factions would notice losing.
quests.subtitle: Team capstone · Mark a service house
quests.title: Free Charter

description: Nessa's first town had no walls, only a bell, dry beds, and a chest nobody was afraid to open. A center becomes real when a lost player can recognize it and understand what may be used.
quests.subtitle: Commons I · A findable center

tasks.title: A teammate found and used the center

quests.title: Town Bell

description: A route is a shared promise that distance will remain understandable. Signs, landmarks, and an archive let the road improve when players discover a safer turn instead of forcing every traveler to relearn it.
quests.subtitle: Commons II · Routes with memory

tasks.title: A teammate followed the marked route

quests.title: Known Roads

description: Oren leaves a chipped wrench above the press with a note: if the line jams, teach the repair to whoever is waiting. The next batch should be easier because two people now know the machine.
quests.subtitle: Commons III · Shared fabrication

tasks.title: A teammate ran one public recipe

quests.title: Common Forge

description: Public architecture does not need a style committee. A modest stone-and-timber palette makes repairs predictable while leaving the shape, history, and odd little details entirely to its builders.
quests.subtitle: Commons IV · Simple public palette

tasks.title: A teammate used the public room

quests.title: Shared Roof

description: The archive is allowed to contain mistakes. Dated photographs and named locations give future players evidence they can correct instead of a perfect story they are expected to obey.
quests.subtitle: Side lane · Places worth remembering

tasks.title: A teammate found one named record

quests.title: Public Archive

description: The watch chest refuses faction ownership. Blood keeps one neighbor alive, holy water protects another, and clear labels let either service reach the road before an argument does.
quests.subtitle: Side lane · Shared emergency stock

tasks.title: A teammate found the emergency stock

quests.title: Night Watch

description: Mirelle leaves one stall empty for the person who arrived with nothing to sell. A good market leaves behind clear prices, working pickup, and a reason to remember who showed up.
quests.subtitle: Side lane · A visible exchange

tasks.title: A teammate read a price and pickup point

quests.title: Market Day

description: Nessa pins one photograph above the bell after every difficult week. The frame is never straight, but the route, service, or shelter in it becomes a dependable beginning for whatever follows.
quests.subtitle: Team capstone · Three public contributions

tasks.title: Have one photograph of the commons

quests.title: First Concord

description: Mirelle keeps six blank invitations because a gathering should fit the people who actually arrive. Each event leaves useful stock or evidence behind, so a small session still changes the world.
quests.subtitle: Events · Complete any three
quests.title: Open Invitation

description: The drill begins where someone once tripped over an unlabeled chest during a real outage. Prepared light and repair stock turn a failure into a shared story that gets less dramatic every time it is practiced.
quests.subtitle: Event · Restore a dark public place

tasks.title: We restored one dark public place

quests.title: Blackout Drill

description: At the red table, neither school is asked to surrender its language. The point is translation: what each preparation protects, what it costs, and who should never receive it by mistake.
quests.subtitle: Event · Compare blood and holy service

tasks.title: We compared both schools at one table

quests.title: The Red Table

description: Oren claims every difficult machine has a moment when four hands are faster than one expert. The event pairs faction benches with public fabrication so players leave with parts, advice, and fewer private bottlenecks.
quests.subtitle: Event · Make equipment together

tasks.title: Two players made one useful set together

quests.title: Four Hands

description: A useful photograph notices what monuments omit: the patched stair, the empty chair, the sign nobody reads. One honest detail can make the archive feel inhabited rather than promotional.
quests.subtitle: Event · Photograph an overlooked place
quests.title: Photo Hunt

description: The relay rewards clean handoffs rather than raw speed. A marked destination, spare transport, and a returned route note make every runner responsible for the person who follows.
quests.subtitle: Event · A route anyone may finish

tasks.title: The next runner finished without guessing

quests.title: Courier Relay

description: Mirelle leaves one chair empty at every auction for the person who decides not to bid. Posted prices and a clean pickup chest make refusal as safe as participation.
quests.subtitle: Event · Trade with visible terms

tasks.title: We held one trade with visible terms

quests.title: Open Auction

description: Three gatherings are enough to reveal what the settlement enjoys doing together. The record names what worked and leaves supplies for the next event instead of prescribing which tradition must continue.
quests.subtitle: Team event · Complete any three
quests.title: Common Cause

description: The board turns quest earnings into choices players can feel in the world. Small purses solve immediate friction; larger denominations fund whole-team projects without pretending every coin is identical pocket change.
quests.subtitle: Weekly services · Team-scoped

tasks.title: I understand prices and team scope

quests.title: Read the Board

description: A small purse replaces the supplies most likely to strand a late arrival. It is deliberately ordinary: food, light, and a way to bring something awkward home.
quests.subtitle: One Bevel · Once per team each week
quests.title: Field Kit

description: The works purse is sized for a visible repair rather than a decorative handful. It supports roads, public rooms, and the unglamorous patch that keeps an old build useful.
quests.subtitle: One Sprocket · Once per team each week
quests.title: Works Kit

description: The arcane purse restocks a teaching table rather than gambling on a random spell. Its materials support several schools and leave the final inscription to the player who understands the need.
quests.subtitle: One Sprocket · Once per team each week
quests.title: Arcane Kit

description: A foundry restock should keep a public line moving through more than one repair. Alloy, brass, and mechanisms buy back time while leaving ore generation and advanced machines valuable.
quests.subtitle: Two Sprockets · Once per team each week
quests.title: Foundry Kit

description: The bond is stamped with a bridge on one face and an empty foundation on the other. Redeeming it puts substantial structural and fabrication stock behind the common project your team chooses.
quests.subtitle: One Cog · Once per team each week
quests.title: Concord Bond

description: After the public events begin, the archive pays for one specific maintenance report: a findable place, a real problem, and the name of whoever will check the result. The written book is consumed as the filed copy.
quests.subtitle: Weekly report · 1 team Bevel

tasks.title: I named the place, problem, and reviewer

quests.title: Rumour Ledger

description: The bank counts base value: a Spur is 1, a Bevel 8, a Sprocket 16, and a Cog 64. Routine work pays Bevels, specialties pay Sprockets, and major team milestones pay Cogs. Crowns and Suns can wait for an economy large enough to deserve them.
quests.subtitle: Coin guide · Spur · Bevel · Sprocket · Cog
quests.title: Know the Coins
